App-user visibility rule: self, own-tenant admins, super admins
Rationale: three overlapping SELECT policies caused unexpected behaviour, so they were folded into one
SECURITY DEFINER self-join escape hatch for app_users RLS
Rationale: policy simplified 'to avoid function call issues' - a policy on app_users that queries app_users needs SECURITY DEFINER to escape recursion
Rationale: 'logged-in users might have a different tenant_id than the tenant they're viewing' (super-admin tenant impersonation)
Decision: the SECURITY DEFINER helper was dropped one hour later, reverting to get_user_tenant_id + get_user_role
Pattern: RLS-by-iteration - policies rewritten wholesale in successive migrations rather than amended
Ledger rows with NULL tenant_id are readable by everyone
Rationale: refund ledger entries are sometimes created with NULL tenant_id, so strict tenant matching hid them
Escalation: NULL tenant_id also accepted on INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, widening the hole from reads to writes
Refundable ledger categories: Tax, Service Fee, Security Deposit
Ledger policies re-scoped TO authenticated; service_role (edge functions) noted as bypassing RLS
Ledger visibility derived from the owning rental's tenant instead of the row's own tenant_id
Rationale: 'get_user_tenant_id() may not be returning the expected value' - the tenant helper itself became suspect
Rental-access oracle: staff-tenant match, super admin, or impersonated tenant
Tenant impersonation carried in JWT user_metadata.impersonated_tenant_id
Decision: RLS turned OFF on ledger_entries entirely
Rationale: ledger is only reached through a rental, rentals have their own RLS, and the ledger policy grew too complex under impersonation
Consequence: ledger tenant isolation is now enforced only by application query shape, not by the database
Manual payment reversal / voiding ('Reversed' status)
Payment status conflates two axes: allocation state (Applied/Credit/Partial) and Stripe lifecycle (Pending/Completed/Refunded)
Tenant-scoped semantic index of operational records (pgvector, 1536-dim OpenAI embeddings)
Trigger-driven change capture: every write to customers/vehicles/rentals/payments/fines/plates enqueues an embedding refresh
Tenant-filtered cosine-similarity retrieval with threshold and table filter
Aggregate business metrics precomputed as RAG context (counts embeddings cannot answer)
Staff AI assistant transcript with cited sources and renderable chart_data
Suspected defect: RAG/chat policies match app_users.id = auth.uid(), while every other tenant policy uses app_users.auth_user_id

Rationale: AFTER triggers run as the caller, so queue_for_rag() tripped rag_sync_queue's service-role-only INSERT policy; SECURITY DEFINER + pinned search_path fixes it safely because tenant_id comes from the triggering row and cannot be spoofed
Blast radius: a broken RAG queue trigger made ordinary rental/customer/vehicle writes fail for authenticated users
Live availability sync: portal edits to blocked dates push to the booking frontend
Vehicle delivery & collection service with per-location fees
Two-level enablement: tenant global toggles gate per-location delivery/collection flags
Rentals snapshot both the location FK and the literal address + fee, so later price or location edits do not rewrite booked history
Unauthenticated booking site reads active locations directly (no auth, is_active as the only filter)
Installment payment plans (full / weekly / monthly) for rentals
Card-on-file: SetupIntent + payment method stored on the plan for off-session recurring charges
Per-tenant installment eligibility rules (min days, max installments) as JSONB
Schedule generation: evenly divides the installable amount and materialises one dated row per installment
Rounding gotcha: installment_amount is ROUND(total/n,2) applied to every row, so the plan can collect slightly more or less than total_installable_amount
Settlement: marks the installment paid, links payment + ledger row, rolls up plan progress and completion
Dunning: failure counter, last failure reason, and promotion to overdue after 3 failures and 3 days past due
Charge selection: only active plans that already hold a Stripe payment method are picked up
Security concern: anon may SELECT and INSERT every installment plan and scheduled installment with USING(true) - added for the unauthenticated booking flow
Daily installment automation: charge due, remind 3 days ahead, sweep overdue
Rationale/gotcha: the pg_cron schedules are commented out and 'must be set up manually in the Supabase dashboard' - this file is not the source of truth for what actually runs
Notification idempotency: UNIQUE(installment_id, notification_type) plus upsert makes re-runs of a cron pass non-duplicating
tenant_id on a notification is derived from the installment's plan by trigger rather than supplied by the caller
Batch overdue sweep - the same 3-failures/3-days rule, reimplemented set-wise
Reminder payload assembled in SQL: customer contact, vehicle and rental number joined for the notification sender
Odometer capture at key handover, denormalised onto the vehicle's current mileage
Rationale: a FOR ALL policy 'may not work correctly for INSERT', so it was split into four per-operation policies
Decision: pickup location tenant isolation moved out of the database - 'app handles tenant validation'
Consequence: any authenticated user of any tenant can select, insert, update or delete any tenant's pickup locations
Bonzah insurance policy lifecycle: quoted, payment_pending, active, cancelled, failed
Rationale: the policy row is created before payment in the booking flow, which is why anon holds INSERT and blanket SELECT
Insurance premium and the winning policy are folded back onto the rental
Five external Bonzah identifiers (quote_id, quote_no, payment_id, policy_no, policy_id) track the quote-to-policy handshake
Tenant-customer chat: one channel per tenant-customer pair
Polymorphic sender: sender_id means app_users.id for staff and customers.id for customers, with no foreign key either way
Chat RLS is the seam between the two auth worlds: staff resolve through app_users, customers through customer_users
Historical note: service_role policies were written 'for Socket.IO server', predating the move to Supabase Realtime
Unread state kept twice: a per-message is_read flag and a per-participant unread_count counter
Decision: chat trigger and helper functions dropped, 'replaced with direct queries in the application code'
Consequence: chat_channels.last_message_at and updated_at lost their triggers and must now be written by the sending client
Super admins can read and write any tenant's chat (support/oversight)
Chat presence: online flag and last_seen_at persisted per participant
Cross-cutting pattern: the unauthenticated booking site forces anon-permissive RLS on every table it touches

hyperedges.label: Seven-migration retreat: ledger_entries RLS tightened, loosened, rewritten, then switched off
Installment lifecycle: plan created, schedule materialised, cron charges card-on-file, row settles to a payment + ledger entry or escalates to overdue with notifications
RAG loop: business-table writes fire a trigger into a queue, embeddings land in rag_documents, retrieval plus aggregate metrics answer the staff assistant
